content: C-C chemokine receptor type 9 (CCR9) is a protein encoded by the CCR9 gene in humans. This receptor has also been designated as CDw199, which stands for cluster of differentiation w199. The protein belongs to the beta chemokine receptor family and is structurally predicted to be a seven-transmembrane domain protein, similar to other G protein-coupled receptors. Chemokines and their receptors, including CCR9, play a critical role in regulating the migration and maturation of thymocytes under both normal physiological conditions and during inflammatory responses. The specific ligand that binds to CCR9 is CCL25, also known as thymus-expressed chemokine (TECK). Research has shown that the expression of the CCR9 gene varies between T lymphocytes located in the small intestine and those in the colon. This differential expression suggests that CCR9 may be involved in the recruitment and development of thymocytes, potentially enabling the immune system to adapt and specialize its responses in distinct regions of the gastrointestinal tract. The CCR9 gene is located within the chemokine receptor gene cluster region of the genome. Additionally, two alternatively spliced transcript variants of this gene have been identified, which may result in different isoforms of the protein with potentially distinct functional roles.
